title: Low back pain and cauda equina
stem: Cubicle 19. Mr Hui, 42, has had low back pain with pain down both legs for 3 days after lifting furniture. Today he noticed difficulty passing urine. Examine his lumbar spine and lower limbs and explain what you would do.

phases.title: Examine
phases.goal: The spine, the legs, and the cauda equina signs.

notes:
Checked against NICE NG59 (Low back pain and sciatica, 2016, updated 2020), the GIRFT national pathway for suspected cauda equina syndrome (2023), and BASS guidance.

Cauda equina syndrome (CES) red flags: bilateral sciatica, saddle or perianal sensory change, bladder dysfunction (retention, altered sensation, loss of desire to void), bowel dysfunction, sexual dysfunction, progressive neurological deficit. Examination: look, feel, move the lumbar spine; straight-leg raise and femoral stretch; lower limb neurology (myotomes, dermatomes, reflexes); perianal sensation and anal tone (digital rectal examination with consent and a chaperone; GIRFT emphasises perianal pinprick sensation); post-void residual bladder scan (residual over 200 mL is concerning). Suspected CES: emergency MRI of the whole lumbar spine (within 4 hours in GIRFT pathway) and spinal surgical referral; decompression within 48 hours of onset (or sooner for incomplete CES) improves outcome.

Your notes list the LS spine exam headings and mention 'incomplete cauda equina syndrome, urinary retention' under HKCEM past topics; nothing conflicts.

steps.label: Examine
steps.hint: Spine, SLR, neurology, saddle sensation, anal tone (chaperone), bladder scan.

Spine.r: Loss of lumbar lordosis, paraspinal spasm, no midline step or bony tenderness.

Nerve root.r: Weak ankle plantarflexion bilaterally (S1), absent ankle jerks both sides, reduced sensation lateral feet.

Saddle.t: Digital rectal examination for anal tone, with consent and a chaperone
Saddle.r: Reduced resting tone; weak voluntary squeeze.
Saddle.mark: Assesses anal tone with consent and chaperone

steps.ask: Thank you. What is your plan?
steps.label: Plan
steps.hint: Suspected CES: emergency MRI, spinal team, catheter.

opts.t: Suspected cauda equina syndrome with retention (CES-R)
Emergency MRI lumbar spine now; urgent spinal surgery referral
Urinary catheter; analgesia; document neurology and timings
Discharge with NSAIDs and GP review
opts.r: Retention with saddle anaesthesia is a surgical emergency.

qs.q: Red flag for cauda equina syndrome?

wrong: Plain X-ray of the lumbar spine
CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
The S1 nerve root and ankle jerk

Only the hip joint and its capsule
A spinal metastasis in every case

badge.name: Saddle Check
badge.flavor: Bilateral sciatica, saddle numbness, retention: MRI now.

options: Bilateral sciatica, saddle anaesthesia, bladder/bowel dysfunction
Unilateral leg pain below the knee
Morning stiffness lasting over an hour
Great toe extension and ankle dorsiflexion
Knee extension, hip adduction and the knee jerk
Ankle plantarflexion, eversion and the ankle jerk

cards.q: Routine imaging for non-specific low back pain?
options: CT of the lumbar spine for all
cards.why: Only with red flags or if it changes management.
Pain radiating below the knee at 30–70°.
